wormald.wormald_date: early eleventh century (English part), appended to a later-eleventh-century manuscript (p. 216); s. xi¹, contemporary with CCCC 190 section a) (p. 220)
wormald.wormald_origin: English script; the host manuscript is from Jumièges (p. 216).
wormald.other_contents: A fragment of the 'Wulfstan Commonplace-book' canon collection in the CCCC 265/Barlow recension, beginning with liturgica and Regularis Concordia extracts; much is lost at the end (only ff. 196–8 of the English final quire survive; f. 199 intrusive) and probably some at the start (p. 216 and n. 208; Table 4.4).
wormald.overview: The Rouen fragment is an early-eleventh-century English copy of part of the Wulfstan canon collection, later attached to a Jumièges MS. It shows the collection at an early stage of arrangement and, with Barlow 37, helps place Corpus 265 within the family; it contains no Anglo-Saxon laws.
wormald.key_quote: Rouen 1382 is a fragment in early-eleventh-century English script appended to a later-eleventh-century manuscript from Jumièges (p. 216)
wormald.doubts: Wormald gives only 'Rouen 1382'; 'Bibliothèque municipale' supplied. Not in the guide; not to be confused with the guide's Rouen 368 (Rj) and 369 (Ro). Aronstam's siglum 'R'. Bears only indirectly on legal texts — include only if useful.
verify_notes: Checked pp. 213, 216 n. 208, 217, 220–1 and Table 4.4 (image: ‘Rouen 1382 (ff. 173r–198v)’, opening with liturgica and Reg. Conc. extracts); checked, no changes.
